title: Calibrated? Not for Everyone: How Sexual Orientation and Religious Markers Distort LLM Accuracy and Confidence in Medical QA

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual insertion of sexual orientation descriptors (e.g., heterosexual, homosexual, gay) into clinical patient vignettes to measure shifts in LLM medical QA accuracy and uncertainty calibration (e.g., semantic entropy, Brier score).
Counterfactual insertion of religious affiliation markers (e.g., Catholic, Muslim, atheist) into clinical patient vignettes to evaluate their impact on model performance and confidence reliability.
Joint insertion of both sexual orientation and religious descriptors into clinical prompts to evaluate the compounded, non-additive distortions in model accuracy and predictive calibration.
